children: Silver prices dropped more than 1% to $53.5 an ounce on Wednesday, reaching their lowest level since November 2025 as the US dollar held near a two-week high following the Federal Reserve’s decision to keep interest rates unchanged.

The FOMC voted 10–2 to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 3.75% to 4.00%, reiterating its commitment to curbing inflation while offering little clarity on the possibility of another hike in December.
Meanwhile, oil prices advanced after an attack on a Saudi Arabian refinery raised concerns over potential supply disruptions.
Geopolitical tensions also intensified after Axios reported that the US and Israel could launch large-scale strikes against Iran unless a last-minute agreement is reached.
According to the CME FedWatch Tool, markets widely anticipate a second Federal Reserve rate hike this year in December.

title: Silver Falls to 2025 Lows
